comment: Both marks lie on the same short recorder jog at its two turns.
P is on the shoulder bend; Q is on the straighter rising stretch below it.
The mark lies within the broad initial rounding of the solid trace.
The mark is at the rounded lower end of the nearly vertical recorder step.
The solid trace changes direction here as it enters the short jog near the grid crossing.
The mark lies on the rounded transition out of the short steep segment.
The mark is on a diagonal stretch below the actual recorder jog.
The mark is on the sloping flank; the distinct jog is above it.
The mark is at the turn from the short vertical step onto the sloping trace.
The mark lies on the rounded turn adjoining the short load step.
The marked segment is straight; the steep jog is farther down and right.
The mark is on the straight diagonal above the jog rather than its end.
The mark is on a sloping segment beyond the small jog.
A small change from the steeper segment to the shallower diagonal occurs at the mark.
The mark is within the shallow shoulder stretch between its more distinct turns.
The trace visibly turns into the steeper side of the shoulder at this mark.
The mark is on the small turn from a steeper segment to a shallower segment.
The trace changes direction at the marked end of the short shallow segment.
Q is inside the thick frame after the separately visible solid trace has merged into it.
Both repeated P samples lie inside the top frame beyond the last distinguishable curve ink.
P lies on the gradual initial bend; Q is farther along the nearly straight dotted stretch.
The dot is on the trace but its neighboring dots follow a nearly straight run at this mark.
The dot is on the trace but is already on the steady rising run beyond the gradual steepening.
The dots maintain essentially the same direction through the mark; no knee is visible there.
P is at the lower tip of the first distinguishable dot within the 2 px allowance.
The first P sample is on the last dot and the second is within 2 px of its tip beside the frame.
Q marks the turn onto the short flat shelf; P is on the straight rise before it.
Q marks the flattening before the step; P is on the straight rise before the later load drop.
Q is at the local load maximum immediately before the visible small drop.
The mark is on the steep initial segment without a visible steepening at that position.
The mark lies on the rounded transition from the initial rise to the lower slope.
The mark is on the rising diagonal beyond the small shoulder rather than at its turn.
The marked stretch is essentially straight; the shoulder turn is elsewhere.
The trace gradually turns into a steeper rise around the mark.
The mark is within the steeper diagonal; its end and flattening are farther up and right.
The solid trace starts rounding into the steeper recorder rise around the mark.
Q lies inside the vertical frame where no separate solid curve ink can be distinguished.
P is inside the right frame beyond the near edge where the solid trace disappears.
P is on the first dash after the rounded turn; Q is on the preceding straight steep dash.
P is on a rising dash after the transition from the shallow trough has already occurred.
Q is inside the left frame; the dashed trace becomes distinguishable to its right.
P marks the rounded entry to the plateau; Q is on the preceding sloping segment.
P is on the kink into the shallow shoulder; Q is within the shallow stretch after the kink.
P is at the start of the small step; Q is on a straight rising stretch farther along.
P is on the turn onto the short shelf; Q is inside the shelf after the turn.
Both lie on the same gradual steepening; the continuous solid stroke can be followed past the thicker dashed endpoint below it.
The continuous solid trace gradually turns upward around the mark; the dashed trace remains separate above it.
The solid trace flattens into a small shoulder at the mark just before the grid crossing.
The mark is on the straight rising segment after the small shoulder has ended.
A small flattening of the continuous solid trace is visible at the mark; the dashed trace is separate below.
P is within the left frame below the point where the solid trace becomes separately visible.
Both Q samples are on the solid trace immediately before it merges into the near edge of the right frame.
P lies on the rounded start of the second rise; Q is on the nearly vertical shoulder before the bend.
P is on the sustained rising dotted segment after its starting bend.
P is inside the frame corner with no separately identifiable dotted trace under it.
Both P samples lie on the final dot which is identifiable by following the dot pattern up to the grid.
Q is at the visible solid trace emergence; continuity from the separate solid stroke identifies it despite dots on its upper edge. P is inside the frame.
P is on the toe bend of the continuous solid stroke; Q is on the straighter stretch. The separate dots approach its upper edge only near P.
P marks the broad plateau entry and Q marks a separate small recorder jog; both are real bends but they are not the same feature.
The solid trace gradually turns away from the near vertical shoulder into the sustained rise at the mark.
The mark is on the sloping stretch below the distinct recorder jog near the grid crossing.
The mark is on the diagonal segment between visible jogs rather than at the end of a jog.
The line turns from the steeper segment into a short shallower jog at the mark.
A small corner into a nearly vertical segment is visible at the mark.
The mark lies on the straight sloping stretch between the visible recorder jogs.
The mark is at the visible corner between the near vertical segment and the short diagonal jog.
The mark is on the sloping approach above the small jog rather than at its turn.
The marked segment is straight between the more distinct changes of direction.
A small transition from the steeper segment to the shallower diagonal is visible at the mark.
Q is inside the frame corner beyond the last separately distinguishable solid trace ink.
P lies on the visible tip of the continuous solid trace above the grid crossing.
